questions.q: A manager asks 'Can I trust the forecast?' What is a strong first answer?
options: Give the number, the range, and how it did on past weeks
Show a list of all metrics
why: Correct: evidence in plain words, with a range and a track record.
A bare yes gives no evidence.

questions.q: Which phrase expresses uncertainty best for a non-expert?
Scenario: the forecast was 1,000 and sales were 1,350, outside your 90% range. What do you say?
options: It is outside our range, so we treat it as an error; the cause was a missing promotion and we now read the promotion calendar daily
The business data is always wrong
why: Outside the range suggests a real problem.
Correct: own the miss, give the cause and the fix.

options: One number, one chart, one action

questions.q: Forecast error fell from 14% to 10%. By how many percentage points did it fall?
questions.why: 14 − 10 = 4 percentage points. (In relative terms it is 4 / 14 = 29% lower.)

questions.q: Scenario: you must present the same forecast to an engineer and to a VP. What changes?
options: The VP gets the decision, the number, the range and the action; the engineer also gets the method and the checks
why: Correct: match detail to the decision the person must make.
